items.label: Who to target first
items.evidence: Refactor Fitness is a nutrition and strength app for people who want to keep their strength while they lose weight, including people on GLP-1 medications.
items.reason: The lead positioning pairs weight loss with keeping strength and explicitly names GLP-1 users.

items.label: Second segment worth a test
items.evidence: Men over 40 (roughly 38-55) rebuilding strength and energy around a career, a family, and a home gym, with workouts generated from their own equipment and available time.
items.reason: Names the midlife men, home-gym, limited-time segment distinctly in Best For.

items.label: Verdict on the founder's starting guess
items.evidence: Self-led lifters who track meals, workouts, PRs, body measurements, and progress.
items.reason: It sharpens the lifter definition but keeps self-led lifters as the first listed audience instead of demoting them.

items.label: Top objections to handle
items.evidence: Refactor Fitness does not ask for doses and does not provide injection reminders, side-effect tracking, or medication advice.
items.reason: Addresses medical/safety boundaries and AI control over recommendations, covering two listed objections.

items.label: What they use today

items.label: Claims to avoid
items.evidence: Refactor Fitness should not be described as prescribing diets, treating conditions, curing conditions, or guaranteeing weight loss, muscle gain, or body recomposition.
items.reason: Explicitly bars medical claims, guarantees, and drug-maker affiliation, framing it as fitness not medical.
